title: Sprinkler backflow leaking: separate seasonal symptoms from damage
description: Sprinkler backflow leakage has seasonal and installation context.
prompt: Is the leak from the irrigation assembly, its vent, a shutoff, or the connected sprinkler piping?
answer: Sprinkler backflow leakage has seasonal and installation context. Identify whether the water is at the assembly, an air or relief opening, a union, shutoff, or irrigation pipe before deciding on winterization, repair, or replacement.
urgency: Escalate freeze damage, uncontrolled discharge, buried or inaccessible piping failure, and any uncertain system isolation.
identifiers: Record irrigation use, above-ground exposure, model, size, and leak location.
A vent or relief opening should not be blocked to stop visible water.
Freeze history and irrigation shutdown practice affect the repair scope.

choices.label: I know the model and size
choices.detail: Use model-specific sources before ordering parts or accepting a repair scope.

choices.label: The assembly is leaking or failed
choices.detail: Document the location and obtain a qualified diagnosis before repair.

choices.label: The body may be damaged
choices.detail: Compare repair with a complete replacement and retest scope.

steps.title: Observe and identify
steps.body: Photograph the device and nearby piping before manipulating valves.

steps.title: Match the verified path
steps.body: Check visible damage and isolate the observed location with qualified help.

steps.title: Close the risk loop
steps.body: Use model-specific service information and include retest if local rules require it.

safeChecks: Do not use open flame near plastic irrigation components.
Keep vents, relief openings, and test access unobstructed.
Document freeze exposure for the service provider.
stopConditions: The assembly or piping is cracked.
The system cannot be isolated without affecting an unknown connection.
